categories.rules: Instructions Claude follows in every session
categories.skills: Reference material Claude loads on demand, or you invoke with /<name>
categories.hooks: Scripts that run around tool calls to enforce the rules
categories.settings: Claude Code preferences merged into settings.json
categories.mcps: External tool servers Claude can call

rules/git.md.details: Conventional Commits (`type: lowercase subject`, 50 chars max, no body, no Co-Authored-By). Branches are `type/slug` off `main`. Never push straight to `main`; force pushes need your OK.

rules/github.md.summary: Pull request and GitHub Actions conventions
rules/github.md.details: PR titles follow the commit format, PRs start as drafts with a 1-2 sentence body and no AI attribution, and GitHub work goes through the GitHub MCP tools instead of `gh`. Workflows must pin every action and image version and use minimal `permissions`.

hooks/block-direct-push.sh.summary: Blocks git pushes to the default branch
hooks/block-direct-push.sh.details: Runs before each Bash command and refuses a `git push` that would land on the default branch — whether by the checked-out branch or by an explicit refspec (`origin HEAD:main`, `+x:refs/heads/main`). Also refuses a push that retargets the repo with `-C`, `--git-dir` or `--work-tree`, since the branch cannot be verified there.

hooks/pr-reminder.sh.summary: Reminds Claude to re-check the PR after a push
hooks/pr-reminder.sh.details: Runs after each Bash command and, following a `git push` on a branch that already tracked an upstream, nudges Claude to confirm the PR description still matches what was pushed. Stays quiet on a branch first push, where there is nothing to refresh yet. Wired with `if: Bash(git *)`, so it is not spawned for non-git commands.

hooks/secrets-guard.sh.summary: Stops Claude reading or editing secret files
hooks/secrets-guard.sh.details: Runs before Read, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit and Bash. Denies paths like `.env`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, SSH keys, `.npmrc` and cloud credential files, and shell commands that read one. Backs up `settings/permissions.json`, covering the notebook paths and shell reads that permission rules do not reach.

settings/attribution.json.details: Sets the commit and PR attribution text to empty and turns off session links, so nothing generated-by is added to git or GitHub content.

settings/model.json.summary: Default model, advisor model and effort levels
settings/model.json.details: Uses Sonnet 5 at medium effort as the main model and Opus 5.5 at high effort as the advisor.

settings/output.json.details: Keeps responses short and result-first instead of the default verbose style.

mcps/github.json.summary: GitHub's hosted MCP server (issues, PRs, code)
mcps/github.json.details: Registers GitHub's official MCP server at `api.githubcopilot.com` so Claude can manage PRs, issues and reviews. Needs `GH_TOKEN` exported in your shell profile, for example `GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token)"`.

rules/comments.md.summary: When to write a code comment, and when not to
rules/comments.md.details: Loads only for source files (`paths` frontmatter). Favours expressing intent in code over commenting; keeps why-not-what notes, consequence warnings and actionable TODOs; rejects restatements, changelog comments, banners, empty docblocks and commented-out code.

skills/twelve-factor.summary: The Twelve-Factor App as review and design rules
skills/twelve-factor.details: All twelve factors turned into directives, for designing or reviewing a deployable service: config in the environment, backing services as attached resources, strict build/release/run separation, stateless processes, port binding, graceful shutdown, dev/prod parity, logs to stdout, one-off admin tasks. Loads on demand or via `/twelve-factor`.

settings/permissions.json.summary: Denies reads and edits of secret files
settings/permissions.json.details: Client-enforced `permissions.deny` rules for `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, SSH keys, `.npmrc`, `.netrc` and cloud credential files. Unlike a rule or hook instruction these are checked by Claude Code itself. Note they also block `.env.example`, which gitignore-style negations cannot carve out of an absolute pattern.

hooks/log-instructions.sh.summary: Logs which rules and CLAUDE.md files loaded
hooks/log-instructions.sh.details: Runs on InstructionsLoaded and appends one line per instruction file to `logs/instructions.log` in the config dir, recording its `load_reason` — `session_start` for an unconditional rule, `path_glob_match` for a `paths`-scoped one. A debugging aid: install it to check a rule is loading when you expect, then uninstall it, since the log grows without bound.
